newsitem.title: USA: Entergy Arkansas 1 nuke at reduced power.
newsitem.headline: Entergy Arkansas 1 nuke at reduced power.

text.p: Entergy Corp's Arkansas 1 nuclear power plant is operating at reduced power following severe storms across the region over the weekend, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Monday.
The unit, rated at 836 megawatts (MW), was operating early Monday at 53 percent of capacity "following (the) loss of transmission lines in Arkansas," the NRC said in its daily status report.
The adjacent unit, Arkansas 2, was still operating at full power. It, too, is rated at 836 MW.
Both units are at Entergy's power generation facility in Russellville, Ark.
Entergy officials were not immediately available to comment on the extent of the damage to local transmission lines or how long the Arkansas 1 unit was likely to be kept at reduced capacity.
A series of tornadoes ripped through the state Saturday, killing at least 24 people and injuring up to 200.
The tornadoes caused extensive structural damage and downed transmission and distribution lines across a 250-mile path from south Arkansas to the state's border with Missouri.
Arkansas officials have requested the White House declare eight of the state's counties disaster areas, a step needed to qualify for federal assistance.
